episode.title: Adapt content-generation client configuration to provider-specific endpoint overrides
episode.before: At parent c5ad0abb5de461416306a516ddbb26dc78f87d40, the content-generator adapter only copied an explicitly supplied config.baseUrl into SDK httpOptions, did not consult GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL or GOOGLE_VERTEX_BASE_URL, did not validate custom endpoint URLs, and forwarded config.vertexai unchanged; consequently provider mode could remain undefined when the selected authentication type identified Vertex AI but credentials had not populated the flag.
episode.after: At cb289e0724b46ce867b6d3fe4bd0ac6ed890dc45, the adapter gives an explicit baseUrl precedence, otherwise selects the endpoint environment variable associated with the authentication type, validates every selected custom URL as parseable and HTTPS except for loopback hosts, passes the resolved URL through SDK httpOptions, and infers the SDK vertexai flag from the selected authentication type when no explicit flag is present.
episode.diff: The implementation adds a custom-base-URL validator, provider-aware environment fallback and explicit-over-environment precedence, plus authentication-type fallback for the SDK provider-mode flag. Seven focused tests cover both provider endpoint variables, provider selection without inferred credentials, precedence, loopback HTTP, malformed URLs, and insecure remote HTTP; existing API-key expectations are updated from an undefined provider flag to false. Configuration documentation adds the two endpoint variables and their security constraints.

evidence_units.claim: Commit cb289e0724b46ce867b6d3fe4bd0ac6ed890dc45 has parent c5ad0abb5de461416306a516ddbb26dc78f87d40, is titled "fix(core): honor GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL and GOOGLE_VERTEX_BASE_URL (#25357)", and changes the implementation, its unit tests, and configuration documentation.
evidence_units.source: issue-bundle.json fields parent_commit, commit_show_stat, changed_files_name_status, and linked_pull_requests[0].commits[0]

evidence_units.claim: The parent implementation constructed httpOptions with config.baseUrl only when explicitly present and passed config.vertexai directly to GoogleGenAI; it contained no custom endpoint validation or provider-specific endpoint environment lookup.
evidence_units.source: git show c5ad0abb5de461416306a516ddbb26dc78f87d40:packages/core/src/core/contentGenerator.ts, ContentGeneratorConfig and createContentGenerator SDK-construction branch

evidence_units.claim: The changed implementation parses custom endpoint URLs and rejects non-HTTPS remote endpoints while permitting localhost, 127.0.0.1, and [::1].

The SDK adapter first uses config.baseUrl; only when it is absent does it select GOOGLE_VERTEX_BASE_URL for Vertex authentication or GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL otherwise, and it validates whichever custom URL is selected.
The resolved endpoint is assigned to httpOptions.baseUrl and supplied to the GoogleGenAI constructor used for API-key, Vertex, and gateway content generation.
When config.vertexai is absent, the adapter now derives the SDK vertexai option from whether authType is USE_VERTEX_AI.

Unit tests assert that the API-key endpoint environment variable reaches SDK httpOptions with vertexai false and that the Vertex endpoint environment variable reaches SDK httpOptions with vertexai true.
A unit test supplies both endpoint variables with Vertex authentication but no inferred Vertex credentials and asserts selection of the Vertex endpoint and vertexai true.
A unit test asserts that an explicitly supplied endpoint takes precedence over the API-key provider's endpoint environment variable.
Unit tests assert that loopback HTTP is accepted, an unparseable custom endpoint is rejected, and remote HTTP is rejected.
Existing API-key client-construction expectations were changed from vertexai undefined to vertexai false, matching authentication-derived provider-mode behavior.
The configuration reference documents both endpoint override variables, their authentication scopes, and the HTTPS-with-loopback-exception rule.

candidate_atomics.name: resolve-provider-specific-endpoint-override
candidate_atomics.description: Resolve a custom service endpoint with explicit configuration taking precedence over the environment variable associated with the selected provider interface, then propagate it into the downstream client options.

semantic_action.intent: Honor endpoint overrides without routing one provider mode through another provider's endpoint or overriding an explicit caller choice.
semantic_action.pre_state: The downstream client accepts an optional endpoint, but the adapter only forwards an explicit endpoint and ignores provider-specific environment overrides.
semantic_action.post_state: The downstream client receives the explicit endpoint when present; otherwise it receives the endpoint override associated with the selected authentication/provider mode.
semantic_action.validation: Constructor-focused tests assert both provider branches, correct selection when both environment variables exist, and explicit-over-environment precedence.

candidate_atomics.name: guard-custom-endpoint-transport
candidate_atomics.description: Validate custom endpoints before client construction, requiring a parseable URL and secure transport except for explicitly allowed loopback development hosts.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent malformed or insecure remote endpoint overrides while preserving local development and proxy use.
semantic_action.pre_state: Custom endpoints can reach the provider SDK without syntax or transport-policy validation.
semantic_action.post_state: Malformed URLs and non-HTTPS remote URLs fail before client construction, while HTTPS endpoints and HTTP loopback endpoints remain admissible.
semantic_action.validation: Negative unit tests assert the malformed-URL and insecure-remote errors, and a positive unit test asserts that loopback HTTP reaches downstream options.

candidate_atomics.name: align-downstream-provider-mode-with-authentication
candidate_atomics.description: Derive the downstream SDK's provider-mode option from the selected authentication type when credential inference has not already set it.

semantic_action.intent: Keep downstream provider behavior aligned with the explicitly selected authentication interface even when credential discovery leaves the provider flag unset.
semantic_action.pre_state: The selected authentication type may identify the cloud-provider interface while the optional downstream provider flag remains undefined.
semantic_action.post_state: An explicit provider flag remains authoritative; otherwise the downstream flag is true exactly for the cloud-provider authentication type and false for other admitted types.
semantic_action.validation: The no-inferred-credentials test asserts cloud-provider mode is still true, while updated API-key tests assert false rather than undefined.

candidate_workflows.name: adapt-provider-client-to-secure-endpoint-overrides
candidate_workflows.description: Extend a provider client boundary so endpoint overrides are selected according to provider mode, respect explicit configuration, pass a transport safety policy, and remain consistent with the downstream SDK's provider-mode switch.

workflow_graph.goal: Construct the downstream provider client with the correct provider mode and a secure endpoint selected from explicit configuration or the matching provider-specific environment override.
workflow_graph.entry_state: A client adapter supports an explicit endpoint and multiple authentication/provider modes, but environment endpoint controls are ignored, endpoint safety is unchecked, and the downstream provider flag can be undefined.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Provider mode is deterministic, endpoint precedence and provider scoping are deterministic, and any selected custom endpoint is validated before being passed to the downstream client.
unresolved_or_deferred: The evidence establishes the adapter's intended unit-test oracle but does not include CI status or an independently executed test result.
Behavior for custom endpoint variables under gateway authentication is not directly tested; the implementation's non-Vertex branch would consult the API-key-provider variable.

unresolved_questions: The GitHub evidence bundle omits the PR body, reviews, comments, and status checks, so motivation and CI outcome beyond the code, commit, and tests are unavailable.
Tests were inspected but not executed because the supplied checkout worktree has its tracked files removed; no validation-pass claim is made.
